les: Mapungubwe vandag: 'n bewaarde plek en 'n eerbewys
kaps_punt: Mapungubwe: eerste staat in Suider-Afrika 1220 - 1300: Vandag: Wêreld Erfenisterrein en die Orde van Mapungubwe

items.bewering: Party plekke is so belangrik vir die hele wêreld dat hulle vir almal bewaar moet word.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, About (whc.unesco.org/en/about): UNESCO seeks to identify, protect and preserve cultural and natural heritage of outstanding value to humanity; World Heritage sites 'belong to all the peoples of the world, irrespective of the territory on which they are located'.

items.bewering: UNESCO, 'n organisasie van lande regoor die wêreld, hou 'n lys van sulke plekke.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, About (whc.unesco.org/en/about): UNESCO is a member-state organisation of the United Nations, and its World Heritage Centre keeps the World Heritage List under the 1972 Convention. A secondary source (University of Oldenburg SEOS page) gives an older count of 191 member states; the lesson gives no number. Technically the World Heritage Committee decides on inscriptions, but 'UNESCO keeps the list' is accurate at this level.

items.bewering: 'n Plek op daardie lys is 'n Wêreld Erfenisterrein.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, About (whc.unesco.org/en/about): a property inscribed on the World Heritage List is a World Heritage site.

items.bewering: UNESCO het die Mapungubwe-terrein op sy lys van Wêreld Erfenisterreine geplaas.
items.bron: UNESCO WHC document 151743 (whc.unesco.org/document/151743) and Koedoe journal (koedoe.co.za, article 89): the Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2003 (property 1099). The inscribed property is called the 'Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape' and is wider than the hill; the lesson gives no year and no area, so 'Mapungubwe-terrein' is accurate.

items.bewering: Die koninkryk self is lank verby, maar die plek is nog daar en word vandag beskerm.
items.bron: SAHistory, Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape (sahistory.org.za/place/mapungubwe-cultural-landscape) and UNESCO WHC document 151743: abandoned in the 14th century. Protected as a national heritage site, declared by SAHRA under section 27 of the National Heritage Resources Act 25 of 1999 (one of the first two declared under that Act, 2001), and as a World Heritage site inside Mapungubwe National Park (SANParks).

items.bewering: Niemand mag sonder toestemming op die terrein grawe of bou nie.
items.bron: SAHRA / SAHRIS permit records for the Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape (sahris.sahra.org.za): work on the national heritage site needs a permit under s27(18) of the NHRA, which forbids destroying, damaging, excavating or altering a heritage site without a permit, and excavation needs a permit under s35(4). Examples: a 2014 excavation permit; a 2024 application for test excavations at Mapungubwe National Park citing s27(18) and s35(4). Building on the site counts as altering it and also falls under national park rules.

items.bewering: So bly die dinge wat nog onder die grond lê, heel vir later.
items.bron: SAHRIS: a 2024 application for ground-penetrating-radar survey and test excavation in Mapungubwe National Park shows archaeological deposits there are still unexcavated, and the permit system exists to keep them from being disturbed. The causal link (protection keeps buried remains intact) is the stated purpose of NHRA s35.

items.bewering: Mense kan die terrein besoek en self sien waar Mapungubwe gestaan het.
items.bron: SANParks, Mapungubwe National Park, Interpretation Centre page (sanparks.org/parks/mapungubwe), and South African Tourism (southafrica.net, 'Mapungubwe: home to Africa's lost kingdom'): visitors tour Mapungubwe Hill with a guide from the park office (the hill is reachable only on a guided tour) and can visit the interpretation centre. The lesson does not say visitors may wander freely, so the claim holds.

items.bewering: Suid-Afrika gee 'n eerbewys met die naam Orde van Mapungubwe. Dit word toegeken aan mense wat iets buitengewoon goed gedoen het.
items.bron: The Presidency, nomination notices for National Orders (presidency.gov.za): the Order of Mapungubwe is awarded to South African citizens 'who have accomplished excellence and exceptional achievements to the benefit of South Africa and beyond'. It is the highest national order, in four classes (platinum, gold, silver, bronze), awarded by the President. 'Mense' is less specific than 'citizens' but not false.

items.bewering: Die land het self hierdie naam gekies.
items.bron: The Presidency, Order of Mapungubwe page (presidency.gov.za/node/5274): 'The central motif for this Order is Mapungubwe'. Artefacts found on Mapungubwe Hill are used in its design. It is a South African national order, instituted by the state (2002, Wikipedia 'Order of Mapungubwe').

items.bewering: Mapungubwe was 'n Afrika-koninkryk hier in Suider-Afrika.
items.bron: The Presidency, Order of Mapungubwe page (presidency.gov.za/node/5274): 'the amazing Kingdom of Mapungubwe' 'existed in the northern corner of South Africa' and 'comprised a sophisticated state system'. Same in UNESCO WHC document 151743.

items.bewering: Die keuse wys dat hierdie koninkryk deel van Suid-Afrika se eie geskiedenis is.
items.bron: The Presidency, Order of Mapungubwe page (presidency.gov.za/node/5274): presents the order's name as honouring an African kingdom that existed in what is now South Africa, citing Wits University that it was 'the most complex society in southern Africa'. Mapungubwe Hill lies in Limpopo, South Africa (SAHRA declaration; SANParks). This sentence interprets the choice of name, and the official framing supports it.

items.bewering: Erfenis is wat uit die verlede oorbly en vandag nog vir mense saak maak.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, About (whc.unesco.org/en/about): 'Heritage is our legacy from the past, what we live with today, and what we pass on to future generations.' The CAPS Gr 4-6 SW KABV, Gr 5 Kwartaal 4 background (printed p. 41), describes heritage as what we inherited from the past, tangible or intangible. The lesson's wording fits both.

items.bewering: Bewaring is nie iets wat vanself gebeur nie. Mense moet elke keer kies om 'n plek of 'n voorwerp op te pas.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, About: World Heritage protection rests on an international treaty that states choose to sign and apply. At Mapungubwe itself, protection depends on a SAHRA declaration and permit decisions taken case by case (SAHRIS permit records). This is a general statement, consistent with how heritage protection works.

items.bewering: 'n Ou plek beteken nie vir almal dieselfde nie: party sien dit as die plek van hul voorouers, en ander wil die verlede leer ken.
items.bron: SAHistory, 'Reburial of Mapungubwe human remains' (sahistory.org.za/dated-event/reburial-mapungubwe-human-remains), and University of Pretoria (Schoeman, 'Repatriating...', 2011; UP news 'Oral history: Mapungubwe uncovered'): several communities (among them Lemba, Vhangona, Tshivhula and Leshiba representatives) claimed descent from the people buried at Mapungubwe, and the remains were reburied there in 2007 after decades of scientific study. That fits both halves of the sentence.

items.bewering: erfenis: Wat uit die verlede oorbly en vandag nog vir mense saak maak.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, About: 'our legacy from the past, what we live with today'. The entry is also accurate read on its own.

items.bewering: bewaring: Om iets op te pas sodat dit nie verlore gaan nie.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, About: to 'identify, protect and preserve' heritage so it can be passed on. This is the ordinary meaning of 'bewaring' (preservation) and is accurate read on its own.

items.bewering: Wêreld Erfenisterrein: 'n Plek wat UNESCO op sy lys van Wêreld Erfenisterreine geplaas het, omdat dit so belangrik vir die hele wêreld is dat dit bewaar moet word. UNESCO is 'n organisasie van lande regoor die wêreld.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, About: sites of 'outstanding value to humanity' inscribed on the World Heritage List; UNESCO is a UN organisation made up of member states. The entry is accurate read on its own.

items.bewering: orde: 'n Eerbewys wat 'n land gee, byvoorbeeld die Orde van Mapungubwe.
items.bron: The Presidency, National Orders (presidency.gov.za): South Africa's national orders, the Order of Mapungubwe among them, are honours the state awards. The entry glosses only the sense this lesson uses. 'orde' has other meanings (neatness, a religious order), and some honour orders are given by monarchs or bodies rather than countries, but the entry does not claim to be the word's only meaning, and its example ties it to this sense.

items.bewering: eerbewys: Iets wat 'n land of groep gee om iemand te eer.
items.bron: This is the ordinary meaning of 'eerbewys' (an honour, a token of honour). The Presidency's national orders are one example from a country. Accurate read on its own.

items.bewering: Mapungubwe: eerste staat in Suider-Afrika 1220 - 1300 (in the lesson's kaps_punt field, not in any block)
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4-6 SW KABV, Gr 6 Geskiedenis Kwartaal 1, printed p. 42: the field quotes CAPS's own heading word for word, and that quotation is confirmed. On the facts: the 1220-1300 span matches the usual dating of the hilltop capital (14th-century abandonment, UNESCO WHC doc 151743, SAHistory). 'Eerste staat' is the traditional view (UNESCO: 'first indigenous kingdom in Southern Africa'), but Chirikure et al. 2014, PLoS ONE 9(10): e111224 (repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/43619), report class distinction and sacred leadership at Mapela Hill, Zimbabwe, about two centuries before Mapungubwe. So the superlative is contested in the literature. No block of THIS lesson repeats it, so it is not a teaching claim here; any sibling lesson that teaches 'eerste staat' in its text needs this checked.

opsomming: Every claim in the lesson text is supported (2003 World Heritage listing, protection and permits, guided visits, the Order of Mapungubwe and the five glossary entries), and it contains no analogies. The only superlative is CAPS's own heading 'eerste staat in Suider-Afrika', quoted in the metadata and not taught here. It is contested by the 2014 Mapela Hill research, so a person should make sure no sibling lesson states it as plain fact.
